chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) remained after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) for seventy-five days, and intense grief had entered her because of her father. Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) used to come to her, console her excellently regarding her father, soothe her soul, inform her about her father and his station, and inform her of what would occur after her among her descendants; and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) would write that down.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام), the angel who came to console and inform her
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.عَزَاءَهَا: his consoling her in her bereavement
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: ʿAlī (عليه السلام), who wrote down what was conveyed
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Kāfī say about Jibrāʾīl’s visits to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) after the Prophet’s passing?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Sayyidah Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) lived for seventy-five days after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) while enduring severe grief over his passing. It states that Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) came to console her, inform her about her father’s station, and convey matters concerning what would happen among her descendants, while Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī (عليه السلام) recorded this.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘(Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup> remained after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for seventy five days, and intense grief entered into her<sup>asws</sup> upon her<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>saww</sup>, and Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> used to come to her<sup>asws</sup> and would excellently console her<sup>asws</sup> upon her<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>saww</sup>, and that would make her<sup>asws</sup> better and he<sup>as</sup> would inform her<sup>asws</sup> about her<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>saww</sup>, and his<sup>saww</sup> place, and he<sup>as</sup> would inform her<sup>asws</sup> with what would be happening after her<sup>asws</sup> among her<sup>asws</sup> children, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> would write that down’.
en.sarwar: Fatima (a.s.) was born five years after the Messenger of Allah declared his message. She died when she was eighteen years and seventy five days old. She lived for seventy five days after the death of her father (s.a).”
